summary: Commonwealth PhD Scholarships are UK Government (FCDO) awards for researchers from 17 eligible Commonwealth countries, including Nigeria, Pakistan, Tanzania and Uganda. They fund a full-time PhD in the UK for up to 36 months: tuition, airfare, a stipend of £1,712 a month (£2,000 in London), fieldwork support, a mid-term home visit and some family allowances. Winners have a strong, feasible research proposal backed by a UK supervisor and a clear development payoff for their country.
lookfor: Academic merit: degree results, transcripts, publications and references
Quality of the research proposal: clear, innovative, relevant, engaged with the literature and feasible in three years
Evidence you have discussed the project with a UK supervisor (signed supervisor statement)
Development impact: the problem, how you will apply new skills, expected change and how you will measure it
Financial need and commitment to return home
cycle: 2027/28: CSC Central closes 20 October 2026 at 16:00 UK time; Nigeria's Federal Scholarship Board advert also gives 20 October 2026. Nominators send nominations to the CSC in December 2026, results by email around July 2027, study starts September/October 2027. The supervisor statement is the hardest part to get quickly — if you cannot get one in time, prepare now for the next round (usually opens in September).

eligibility.q: Are you a citizen and permanent resident of one of the 17 eligible countries (e.g. Nigeria, Bangladesh, Pakistan, Rwanda, Sierra Leone, Tanzania, Uganda, Zambia)?
eligibility.no: Ghana, Kenya and India are not on the PhD list. Consider Gates Cambridge, university PhD studentships or the Commonwealth Master's if your country qualifies.

eligibility.q: Do you have a 2:1 first degree, or a 2:2 plus a relevant postgraduate qualification (usually a master's)?
eligibility.no: Complete a relevant master's first. Nigeria's FSB advert asks PhD applicants for a relevant master's plus at least a 2:2.

eligibility.q: Have you NOT registered for a PhD or MPhil before September 2026?
eligibility.no: You are not eligible; the award does not fund the remainder of a PhD already started.

eligibility.q: Can a UK supervisor at your chosen university sign a supporting statement before the deadline?
eligibility.no: Start contacting supervisors now and aim for the next round.

eligibility.q: Could you afford a UK PhD without this award?
eligibility.no: If yes, you are not eligible — financial need is required.

eligibility.q: Nigeria only: do you have your NYSC certificate or exemption?
eligibility.no: FSB requires NYSC evidence; finish NYSC first.

steps.title: Confirm eligibility and your nominator
steps.why: You must be nominated, and you must meet both the CSC rules and your nominator's rules.
do: Open the Commonwealth PhD page and check the country list and degree rule.
Open the national nominating agencies list and find your body (Nigeria: Federal Scholarship Board).
Read your nominator's advert and note extra documents and its deadline.
Use the earlier of the two deadlines as yours.
tips: Disabled applicants without a 2:1 may apply through the Commonwealth Disabled People's Forum nominator.
avoid: Assuming the CSC deadline is the only one.
check: I know my nominator, its deadline and its document list.

steps.title: Learn how proposals are judged
steps.why: The research proposal is judged on clarity, engagement with the literature and with your supervisor, innovation, relevance and feasibility in three years.
do: Open the selection criteria page and read the doctoral section.
Write the criteria as a checklist at the top of your proposal draft.
Write your research problem and its development relevance in two sentences.
tips: Feasibility matters: data access, fieldwork and ethics must be realistic for 36 months.
avoid: A topic so broad it needs ten years.
check: I can explain my research question and why it matters for my country in under a minute.

steps.title: Find and contact UK supervisors
steps.why: A signed supervisor statement from at least one of your named universities is required. Without it your application fails.
do: Use the CSC UK university list, then search department pages for academics publishing on your topic.
Read two recent papers by each and shortlist five supervisors.
Email each: a three-line introduction, a one-page proposal summary, your CV, and a clear ask: 'Would you consider supervising this for a Commonwealth PhD Scholarship application due 20 October?'
Follow up once after ten days.
When one agrees, revise the proposal with their comments.
tips: Mention specific papers of theirs and how your work builds on them.
Ask early — supervisors receive many such emails in September and October.
check: At least one supervisor has agreed to write a statement.

links.t: Example: Sussex advice on supervisor statements

steps.title: Apply to the universities for PhD admission
steps.why: Universities often need your PhD application before the supervisor can write the statement, and Nigeria's FSB advert asks for UK admission letters from at least two institutions.
do: Apply through each university's PhD portal (CV, transcripts, proposal, references, English evidence).
Tell the admissions team you are applying for a Commonwealth PhD Scholarship.
Upload any offer letters to your CSC application.
tips: Some universities have no internal deadline but still advise applying as early as possible.
avoid: Leaving the university application until after the CSC deadline.

steps.title: Set up CSC Central and draft from the template
steps.why: Answers cannot be edited after submission. Drafting from the template avoids lost work.
do: Download the PhD template form 2027 and the guidance document.
Register on CSC Central and set up two-factor authentication.
Select your nominating body.
Copy each question into a working document.
tips: Save early and often in the portal.
check: My account works and my nominator is selected.

steps.title: Collect transcripts, ID and Nigeria-specific documents
steps.why: Missing or incomplete transcripts make the application ineligible.
do: Request complete certified transcripts for your bachelor's and master's from each university's registry or transcript portal (budget the naira fees).
Scan your passport or national ID photo page as a PDF.
Nigeria: scan NYSC certificate, birth certificate and a passport photograph for FSB.
Scan any UK admission letters.
Check every PDF includes all pages.
tips: Ongoing studies need a to-date transcript.
check: Every transcript is complete and readable.

steps.title: Write the research proposal (study plan)
steps.why: Proposal quality is a main selection criterion.
do: Title and research question(s), with aims and objectives.
Background: what is known, the gap, and why it matters for your country (cite key work).
Methods: design, data, sites, analysis, ethics.
Timeline across 36 months, including fieldwork.
Expected outputs and development relevance.
Ask your supervisor to read it before you submit.
tips: Show you have engaged with your supervisor's work.
State exactly where fieldwork will happen and why it is feasible.
avoid: A literature review with no clear question or method.
check: A reader from another field understands the question, method and payoff.

links.t: Watch: Developing your PhD proposal and making an application (University of Glasgow College of Arts & Humanities)
Watch: PhD research proposal | 5 *essential* elements to make it AWESOME (Andy Stapleton)

steps.prompt: Detailed study plan / research proposal: question, background, methods, timeline and feasibility.
steps.limit: Check the PhD template form for the current word limit.

steps.title: Write the development impact statement
steps.why: Development impact is one of the three selection criteria.
do: Part 1: the development issue at global, national and local level, linked to a CSC theme.
Part 2: how you will apply new skills after the award.
Part 3: expected outcomes, timeframe and beneficiaries.
Part 4: how you will measure and evidence the change.
tips: Name the institutions in your country that will use your research.
avoid: Promising national transformation from one PhD.
check: Each part has concrete, measurable content.
steps.prompt: Four parts: the issue; applying new skills; expected outcomes, timeframe and beneficiaries; measurement.
steps.limit: Separate limits per part — check the template form.

steps.title: Write career plans, personal statement and leadership summary
steps.why: These show who you are and how the PhD fits a career at home.
do: Award objectives: what you want from the scholarship and how it meets them.
Career plans: five-year and long-term, with named roles and institutions.
Personal statement: your background, motivation and contribution to development.
Voluntary and leadership activities: specific roles, dates and results.
List up to 10 publications and prizes in the form.
tips: Lecturers: name the courses you will teach and the lab you will build on return.
avoid: Inconsistency between career plans and development impact.
check: All sections tell the same story.
steps.prompt: Personal statement on background, motivation and development contribution; career plans; voluntary and leadership activities.

steps.title: Get references and the supervisor statement as signed PDFs
steps.why: You upload all supporting documents yourself. Missing ones mean ineligible.
do: Ask at least two referees who know your academic and research work (e.g. master's supervisor, head of department).
Send them your proposal summary and development statement.
Ask for a signed PDF on letterhead, or an email showing official details, covering your academic ability, strengths and weaknesses and development potential.
Ask your UK supervisor for a signed statement confirming willingness to supervise, facilities, fit and feasibility in 36 months.
Upload all PDFs in CSC Central.
tips: Give referees a deadline a week before yours.
avoid: Unsigned letters or plain Word files.
check: Two references and the supervisor statement are uploaded.

steps.title: Complete and submit before 20 October
do: Paste final answers into every section.
Check your three ranked university/supervisor choices.
Confirm every PDF opens and is complete.
Submit before 16:00 UK time and save the confirmation.
Nigeria: print the completed application PDF for the FSB interview.
tips: Submit two or three days early.
check: I have a confirmation and a printed copy.

steps.title: Prepare for nominator screening and interview
steps.why: Your nominator decides who goes forward to the CSC.
do: Watch email and FSB / Ministry of Education notices.
Bring the printed application, original certificates, NYSC certificate and ID.
Practise a three-minute talk on your question, method and impact.
Prepare for questions on feasibility, ethics and why the UK.
tips: Contact fsb@education.gov.ng if dates approach and you have no news.
check: I can defend my method and timeline.

steps.title: Results, offer and pre-departure
steps.why: Results arrive by email around July 2027; offers lapse if you do not reply in time.
do: Check email including spam from spring 2027.
Reply to the CSC within the time stated.
Secure the unconditional PhD offer and apply for your student visa.
Read the CSC handbook on stipend, fieldwork and family allowances.
tips: Keep your supervisor updated on your result.
avoid: Changing university or topic after selection — the CSC will not usually allow it.

faq.a: Not for the CSC, but your university may require it.

faq.q: Do I need an admission offer to apply?
faq.a: The CSC does not require one, but you need a supervisor statement, and Nigeria's FSB advert asks for UK admission letters.

faq.q: Is Ghana or Kenya eligible for the PhD award?
faq.a: Not in 2027/28; the PhD list has 17 countries. Check the official list.
No CSC fee; universities may charge application fees.
Yes; spouse and child allowances may apply under CSC rules.
